newsitem.title: INDIA: Mobil says to set up Indian subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Mobil says to set up Indian subsidiary.

text.p: U.S.-based Mobil Corp said on Monday that the Indian government had approved its proposal to set up a wholly-owned subsidiary with an initial investment of $5 million.

Mobil's representative in India, Craig Murphy, told Reuters that the Foreign Investment Promotion Board had cleared the formation of the subsidiary, Mobil India, which will coordinate Mobil's existing joint venture activities in India.

Murphy is also chief executive of Indo Mobil Ltd, a 50:50 joint venture between Indian Oil Corp (IOC) and Mobil that was set up in 1994 to blend, package and market Mobil-brand lubricants and greases in India.
Indo Mobil also markets products in Nepal and Bhutan.
"The intention of Mobil India is to provide support to our joint venture," Murphy said. "The initial investment in this company is $5 million."
India's lubricant market is estimated at about one million tonnes a year, Murphy said in an interview last month. He declined to give Mobil's share of the lubricant market.

Mobil, along with India's Pennar group and the Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation (TIDCO), is setting up a five-million-tonne oil refinery at a total cost of $750 million in the southern state of Tamil Nadu.
The equity ownership of the refinery has not yet been established, Murphy said.
Mobil is one of 17 companies that have put in bids to participate in a public sector consortium to distribute liquefied natural gas (LNG) in India.
